title: appveyor: run tests again
body:
- in jobs building tests, also run them.
- to maintain CI cycle times, only run unit tests by default, and run
  all (supported) tests in just one job, carefully selected to be the
  one running them the fastest.
  Per job, it takes ~15 seconds to run ~80 unit tests.
  It takes 5 minutes to run all (~1600) tests. Total job time 5.5-6
  minutes.
  If the full test run turns out to be annoying or grow slow, we disable
  or limit it to a subset of tests.
- run tests with `-j10` parallelism. It results in the fastest runs,
  based on tests.
- to avoid the MSBuild test breaker heuristics, and to improve
  performance, run tests by directly invoking `runtests.pl` (not via
  CMake → MSBuild → `runtests.pl`).
  It saves 10-40 seconds per full test run.
- when running directly via `runtests.pl`, exclude test 1119 and 1167.
  It's not compatible with Visual Studio generator builds.
- run the artifact upload in parallel with running tests.

Running Windows tests in multiple environments makes it more likely they
can run on local machines, too, also making them easier to debug.
AppVeyor also supports remote access via RDP, which may help debugging
notorious Windows issues live, with some luck of reproducing it in a run
with RDP access explicitly enabled beforehand.

---

[ Note: No LLMs were used for these investigations, nor to develop
solutions. (I used Copilot for PR review in some cases.) ]

Another post-commit note: 400 tests (20%) are skipped for whatever
reasons and still not run after this patch. Notably missing are HTTPS
ones. Future effort can fix some of these; the ultimate limit is obtaining
dependencies for MSVC builds. On Windows this remains an incredibly
difficult and/or time-consuming task. vcpkg can do it, but needs to
build everything from scratch (no cache or pre-built binaries!), which
in practice makes it a no-go. With VS2015+ it's possible to reuse prebuilt
MSYS2 libs, but also not just a flip of a switch, most likely. Things for
the future, if it's worth it. First, it'd be nice to stabilize the infrastructure
I think, and it's not at all trivial this will happen anytime soon.

---

With default -j20, it takes around 21 seconds to run the ~80 unit tests.

Caveat: Thanks to the undisablable MSBuild heuristics unpredictably
flagging valid test runs as failed depending on their log output,
enabling tests in AppVeyor may re-introduce this issue to the CI. In GHA
the solution was to avoid MSBuild. That workaround is not generic and
unpractical for AppVeyor, and we'd also like to continue testing builds
with MSBuild. The issue has been mitigated, and expected to  happen
rarely, but it isn't and cannot be fixed 100% when using this build
tool. This is further mitigated by running only a limited set of tests
in AppVeyor CI.

- [ ] perhaps look at build perf again: appbuild? File tracking?
- [x] perhaps I discarded this idea earlier, but maybe try to fix the MSBuild heuristics, by NOT launching runtests via CMake, and do it directly instead. Ensure Perl, the env, and arguments are identical.
  → test 1119 is one gotcha here. and 1167. These two tests are a time-sink, I wonder if there is another way.
  wow, removing MSBuild from this step saves 20-40 seconds per job with -j10 and all tests.
  Bef: https://ci.appveyor.com/project/curlorg/curl/builds/54913825
  Aft: https://ci.appveyor.com/project/curlorg/curl/builds/54917936
- [x] tweak -j20 to optimum? → -j10
- [x] decide which tests run, and in which jobs
- [x] rebase on remaining split off PRs
- [x] localize the local-bool-type/bitfield confusion. Which VS versions? Is it VS only?
  how does the CRT define bool? find/use smallest workaround.
- [x] split off and finalize long-term useful improvements developed within the PR.
  (CRTDBG, AppVeyor CI RDP option, config support, debug stuff, artifact upload minor improvements; document AppVeyor CI runner details, dedupe DLL list dumper code into curlx/toolx)
  → #23396
  → #23400

- [x] GetLoadedModulePaths → rename to avoid to Win32 API-look,
  move to toolx, print directly (drop slist), reuse from src and libtests/first.
- [x] runtests: perhaps try fixing to not allow lingering forever if there is
  stuck job? force-kill after a while? (= taskkill /f on Windows) → #23488 (report)
- [x] try RDP-ing live a crashed Perl session like:
  https://ci.appveyor.com/project/curlorg/curl/builds/54868825/job/r9ldgbtd36q8e9g4
  https://ci.appveyor.com/project/curlorg/curl/builds/54869181/job/hv88edlb1rnwp7ut
  (1 such job per run, in these 2 runs. Maybe possible to catch one live?) → added a note about this to the "megathread" of Windows problems: https://github.com/curl/curl/discussions/14854#discussioncomment-19034666

@@ -140,7 +140,7 @@ if [[ "${CREATE_ARTIFACT:-}" = 'true' ]]; then
   echo 'Creating artifact'
   time 7z a "${archive}" -y -bb1 -bsp0 -tzip -i@files.tmp curl-ca-bundle.crt WARNING.txt
   rm files.tmp
-  appveyor PushArtifact "${archive}"
+  appveyor PushArtifact "${archive}" &
 fi
 
 # build tests
@@ -161,6 +161,24 @@ if [ -n "${CMAKE_GENERATOR:-}" ] && [[ "${APPVEYOR_JOB_NAME}" = *'Build-tests'*
       "_bld/tests/tunit/${PRJ_CFG}/tunits.exe" --dump-module-paths | sort -f
       "_bld/tests/unit/${PRJ_CFG}/units.exe" --dump-module-paths | sort -f
     fi
+
+    # run unit tests
+
+    unset APPVEYOR_API_URL  # disable updating the 'Tests' counter via the API to save CI time
+    TFLAGS="~1096 ${TFLAGS:-}"
+    if [ -n "${RUN_TESTS_VIA_CMAKE:-}" ]; then  # just to document the differences
+      export TFLAGS="-j10 ${TFLAGS}"
+      time cmake --build _bld --config "${PRJ_CFG}" --target test-ci
+    else
+      export CURL_DIRSUFFIX="${PRJ_CFG}"
+      TFLAGS="!1119 !1167 ${TFLAGS:-}"  # skip tests that need a configured cl.exe
+      (
+        cd _bld/tests
+        # This command must use the same Perl as detected in the CMake configuration step.
+        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+        time ../../tests/runtests.pl -a -p ~flaky ~timing-dependent -r --retry=5 -j10 --buildinfo ${TFLAGS:-}
+      )
+    fi
   else
     echo "Skip running tests. Reason: ${SKIP_RUN}"
   fi
